// types: var declarations, inference, numeric conversion, zero values.
var count int32;
count = 41;
assert.Equal(tb, "41", fmt.Sprintf("%d", count));

x = 2.5;
assert.Equal(tb, "2.5", fmt.Sprintf("%v", x));

var u url.URL;
assert.Equal(tb, "", u.Path);
assert.True(tb, true);

// A conversion hint fixes a literal's type at the assignment, the
// way a var declaration would.
y = int32(7);
assert.Equal(tb, "int32", fmt.Sprintf("%T", y));
assert.Equal(tb, "7", fmt.Sprintf("%d", y));

f = float32(1.5);
assert.Equal(tb, "float32", fmt.Sprintf("%T", f));

// The hinted type sticks: a later assignment converts to it.
y = 9;
assert.Equal(tb, "int32", fmt.Sprintf("%T", y));
